title: Validate path containment at every mutation site for manifest-driven operations
context: Wiki manifest is committed (making page keys PR- and merge-influenceable), yet every key drives file write/delete operations. Traversing keys like '../../id_rsa' enabled arbitrary file deletion without per-site validation. Touches invariant(s): con_e04226bd05 (The MCP server must stay client-agnostic: all assistants point to the same .hunch/ graph; no Claude-only behavior in the server).
decision: Introduce containedPagePath() to independently verify that a page key resolves within the wiki directory. Call it at write, delete, and orphan-classification sites. Reject unsafe --dir overrides at parse time. Paths written before this guard still cannot escape.
consequences: Arbitrary file deletion via manifest key traversal is now impossible even if upstream filters fail or pre-date the fix
Per-site validation eliminates reliance on a single upstream filter; each mutation independently confirms safety
Unsafe --dir overrides fail loudly (throw) instead of silently falling back, making intent explicit
Manifests committed before this guard was added are still safe (backward-compatible containment)
alternatives_rejected: Validate only at wikiStatus intake — leaves delete site vulnerable to manifest-driven exploitation
Silently ignore escaping keys — hides errors and remains fragile if logic evolves
Validate at write time only — asymmetric defense, leaves orphan deletion unguarded
Default to silently falling back on unsafe --dir — caller never learns their intent was rejected
